items.q: We send only a domain to check it — never your full URLs or page content. Privacy is the architecture, not a marketing checkbox.
We publish our phishing-detection rate every week — the exact script, the exact dataset, side by side with Cloudflare and Google. Measured, not marketed.
Core link-blocking is free forever. We only charge for extras like family protection and detailed explanations — never for the protection itself.

items.a: Your browsing history never leaves your device. Our servers store only your email and subscription status. Even if we're breached, attackers learn nothing about your online activity.
No. Most domains resolve instantly against an on-device safe-list. Only unknown domains are sent to our API, and we send only the domain name — never the full URL.

items.q: Can I use it with a VPN?
items.a: Yes! On mobile, Cleanway auto-detects your VPN and switches to DNS mode, working alongside NordVPN, ExpressVPN, or any other provider.

items.q: What's different from Google Safe Browsing?
items.a: Google Safe Browsing is reactive — it catches known threats but misses new phishing. Cleanway adds an ML detection signal, ~15 more threat-intelligence sources, Privacy Audit, and doesn't send your browsing history to Google.
Yes! The free plan includes 10 API checks/day for unknown domains, unlimited instant checks against the on-device safe-list, and basic Privacy Audit. Most casual users never need to upgrade.
Business plan includes simulated phishing emails sent to your team. Pick a template, we send test emails, track who clicks vs. who reports. For training, not punishment.

dns.page_title: Phishing-blocking DNS — one tap, no app
dns.page_description: Install Cleanway's phishing-blocking DNS resolver in 30 seconds on iPhone, Android, Mac or Windows. System-wide protection without a VPN or an app.
dns.hero_title: Block phishing on every app — without installing one
dns.hero_subtitle: Cleanway runs a phishing-blocking DNS resolver. Point your phone or laptop at it and every app on the device — Safari, Chrome, Mail, banking apps — gets the same protection.
dns.hero_meta: Works on iOS 14+, iPadOS 14+, macOS 11+, Android 9+, Windows 11. No VPN. No battery hit.
dns.ios_intro: Tap the button below on your iPhone or iPad. iOS will ask permission to install a configuration profile.
dns.ios_step1: Tap “Allow” when iOS asks to download the profile.
dns.ios_step2: Open Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → Cleanway DNS.
dns.ios_step3: Tap “Install” twice, then enter your device passcode.
dns.ios_unsigned_note: If iOS shows “Unsigned”, that’s expected — Apple’s signing program is paid and we’d rather not pass the cost on to you. The profile itself is unchanged whether it’s signed or not.
dns.android_intro: Android 9 (Pie) and later have built-in DNS-over-TLS — no app required.
dns.android_step1: Open Settings → Network & internet → Private DNS.
dns.android_compat_note: Some Samsung and Xiaomi devices nest the option under Connections → More connection settings. Search “Private DNS” in Settings if you can’t find it.
dns.win_intro: Windows 11 supports DNS-over-HTTPS natively. Earlier Windows versions need a third-party tool like Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 — sorry.
dns.win_step1: Open Settings → Network & internet → Wi-Fi → click your network → DNS server assignment → Edit.
dns.win_step2: Switch to Manual, turn on IPv4, set preferred DNS to 1.1.1.1 with DNS over HTTPS “On (manual template)”.
dns.benefits_heading: What does this protect me from?
dns.benefit_1: Phishing links in SMS, email, and Telegram open as a “site not found” instead of a credential-stealing page.
dns.benefit_2: Known malware command-and-control hosts are stopped before your phone can reach them — as long as they are on the list.
dns.benefit_3: Brand-impersonation domains (paypal-secure-login.com) are blocked at the resolver level — your browser never even loads them.
dns.benefit_4: Works on every app, not just your browser. WhatsApp links, banking apps, in-app browsers — all protected.
dns.privacy_heading: Privacy — what we see and what we don’t
dns.privacy_body: Cleanway DNS resolves the domain only. We never log the queries to disk, never send them to Sentry, never sell them to anyone. Queries stay in memory just long enough to answer the request.
dns.privacy_logs: What we DO keep: an anonymous daily counter of total queries and total blocks, used to publish our quarterly transparency report. No domains, no IPs, no users.
dns.layer_heading: Where DNS fits in your protection
dns.layer_body: DNS is the widest layer — it protects every app on your device, not just the browser. It is also the shallowest: it can only block a domain that is already on our phishing blocklist. It cannot read a page, so on its own it will not catch a brand-new phishing kit the moment it appears, or a credential form hiding on a trusted-but-hacked site.
dns.layer_extension: For that deeper protection, add the Cleanway browser extension. It runs the full per-page analysis on every site you open, spots look-alike login forms in real time, and warns you before you type a password. DNS covers the widest surface; the extension adds the deepest checks — together they cover both.
dns.layer_generic: This is not a generic DNS filter. Cleanway DNS is tuned specifically for phishing and credential theft, driven by the same threat intelligence that powers the extension — not a repurposed ad-blocking list.

methodology.page_description: Cleanway's per-domain detection results vs Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 for Families, Google Safe Browsing, PhishTank, and VirusTotal — measured weekly on fresh URLhaus + PhishTank URLs. Reproducible benchmark script linked.
methodology.hero_title: How we measure our own detection rate
methodology.hero_subtitle: Every recall number we publish points here. The dataset, the script, and a button to clone it on GitHub.
methodology.why_p1: Every other anti-phishing vendor publishes glossy quarterly threat reports without their false-positive rate or per-vendor recall comparison. The numbers exist only in their internal dashboards.
methodology.why_p2: We do the opposite: this page runs the same Python script anyone can clone, every Monday, against fresh URLhaus + PhishTank phishing URLs, and publishes the raw results. The script's output IS the marketing claim.
methodology.results_unavailable: Latest benchmark snapshot not available — re-running cron now.
methodology.results_meta: Snapshot: $DATE$. Sample: $PHISHING$ phishing URLs, $LEGIT$ Tranco legit URLs.
methodology.safe_table_heading: Legit batch (FPR — false-positive rate, expected verdict: safe)
methodology.verdict_mapping_heading: How we map each resolver's response
methodology.verdict_mapping_p1: Different vendors return different verdict shapes. We normalise to three: dangerous / safe / unknown. Unknown verdicts (rate-limited, not indexed, error) are reported separately — not counted as right or wrong.
methodology.reproduce_p1: Two commands and a Python 3 install. The script fetches the same feeds, runs the same comparisons, writes the same JSON output:
methodology.cadence_p1: The benchmark runs every Monday at 05:15 UTC via a GitHub Actions cron. Results commit to docs/benchmarks/ in this repo. A regression-detection step opens a PR if recall drops more than 5 percentage points week-over-week.
methodology.caveat_1: Cleanway uses the public /api/v1/check endpoint — same anonymous surface a regular user would see. We deliberately do NOT use a privileged path for benchmarking ourselves.
methodology.caveat_2: PhishTank's free check API returns 'not indexed' for most fresh URLhaus URLs because their database lags by a few hours — that's why PhishTank's Recall column often shows '—' (unknown), not because it's broken.
methodology.caveat_3: Google Safe Browsing requires an API key (GOOGLE_SAFE_BROWSING_KEY). If unset, that column shows '—' and is excluded from the comparison.
methodology.caveat_4: Latency p50 measured from this script's host (US/EU CI runner); your latency from Asia or LATAM will differ. The relative comparison stays the same.

support.q_vpn: Is this a VPN that hides my traffic?
support.a_vpn: No. Cleanway sets up a local filter on your phone to block scam sites in every app. It is not an anonymity VPN — it does not hide where you go or route your traffic through another country. Website lookups it doesn't block go to a normal public resolver, the same way your phone already works.

support.a_privacy: The shield matches website names on your phone — nothing about the sites you visit is sent to us. See our privacy page for the full detail.

disclosure.title: How the shield works
disclosure.body:
Cleanway sets up a local VPN on your phone. That is how Android lets an app filter website lookups for every other app.

• The list of known scam sites is stored on your phone. Website names are matched here, not sent to us.
• Lookups we don't block go to a public resolver (Cloudflare or Quad9), the same way your phone already works.
• No other traffic is read, recorded or redirected. It is not a privacy VPN and does not hide your browsing.

Android will now ask you to allow the connection.

settings.alerts_note: The shield tells you when it stops a dangerous site. The switches above are not built yet, and Cleanway never watches your clipboard.
settings.push_desc: Tell me when a link looks dangerous
settings.auto_check_desc: Check a link as soon as I share it to Cleanway
settings.weekly_desc: Send me a summary once a week
settings.clear_confirm_body: This deletes every check saved on this phone. It cannot be undone.
settings.privacy_note: Your check history stays on this phone. When you check a link, only the website name goes to our servers.
settings.sync_failed_body: We couldn't reach your account, so this change won't show on your other devices yet. It will sync next time you change it while online.
settings.clear_done_body: All saved checks were removed from this phone.
settings.clear_failed_body: Something went wrong — your history is unchanged. Please try again.
settings.allowed_desc: Sites you marked as safe. The shield does not block these.
settings.allow_confirm_body: {{domain}} will not be blocked until you remove it here. Only do this if you know the site.
settings.language_note: Choose the language for the app.
settings.language_reload_body: Please close and reopen the app to finish switching the layout direction.
settings.linkguard_note: When on, Cleanway checks every link you tap — in any app — and warns you before a scam page opens. Safe links open straight away.
settings.linkguard_on_desc: Every link you tap is checked first.
settings.linkguard_off_desc: Right now links open without a check. Turn this on to check them.

family.title: Family Hub
family.signed_out_body: Sign in to set up Family Hub. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, you get an alert — end-to-end encrypted, so not even Cleanway can read it.
family.load_failed_body: We couldn't reach our servers, so we can't show your family right now. Your family is still there — please try again.
family.no_family_body: Get an alert when a scam is blocked in a loved one's browser. End-to-end encrypted — even Cleanway can't read the alerts.
family.join_invalid: That invite is not valid or has expired. Codes match upper and lower case exactly — pasting is the safest way.
family.members_load_failed: Couldn't load the member list right now. It usually comes back on its own — check again in a moment.
family.invite_desc: Makes a one-time code and PIN. Send them by text or read them out. Both appear once — keep them where the other person can read them.
family.alerts_empty: No alerts yet. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, it shows up here.
family.alerts_load_failed: Couldn't load alerts right now. This does not mean there are none — please try again.
family.alerts_undecryptable: {{n}} alert(s) couldn't be read on this phone. They were sent to a key this device doesn't have.
family.modal_title: Share this with your family member
family.modal_desc: Both appear once. After this closes you can't see them again — make another invite if you need to.
family.join_network_failed: We couldn't reach our servers, so the code wasn't checked. Your invite is fine — try again in a moment.

auth.sub_login: Sign in to keep your settings on all your devices
auth.sub_register: Free to start — no card needed for an account
auth.sub_reset: We'll email you a link to set a new password
auth.switch_to_register: Don't have an account? Sign up
auth.switch_to_login: Already have an account? Sign in
auth.privacy: With or without an account: we check website names on our servers — never your passwords, messages, or browsing history.
auth.confirm_body: We sent a confirmation link. Open it to activate your account.
auth.reset_sent_body: If an account exists for this address, we've sent a link to reset your password.
auth.generic_error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
auth.not_configured: Sign-in isn't available in this build. You can use everything else without an account.
auth.otp_sub: Enter your email and we'll send you a login code
auth.err_code_wrong: Wrong or expired code. Request a new one.

onboarding.s1_title: Check anything before you tap it
onboarding.s1_desc: Paste a link, scan a QR code, or share anything suspicious straight to Cleanway. You get a plain answer and the reasons behind it.
onboarding.s2_desc: To check a link, only the website name is sent to our servers — never your passwords, messages, or browsing history.
onboarding.s3_desc: On Android, one setup step blocks known scam sites in every app. Brand-new scams can slip past any blocklist — that's what the check button is for.

android_native.fg_channel_desc: Shown while phishing protection is active
android_native.block_channel_desc: Tells you when a dangerous site was stopped
android_native.blocked_text: {{domain}} looked like a scam, so it was stopped before it could open.
android_native.warn_title: This site looks like a scam
android_native.warn_text: {{domain}} looks dangerous. If it is open, close it and don't type anything.
android_native.allowed_text: {{domain}} is allowed now. You can undo this in Settings → Allowed sites.

reason.flagged_dangerous: Google flags this site as dangerous
reason.on_blocklists: On trusted scam and spam blocklists
reason.imitates_brand: The name imitates a well-known brand
reason.lookalike_letters: Uses look-alike letters to fool you
reason.fake_brand_address: A trusted brand name is hidden inside a fake address
reason.raw_ip_address: The address is a raw number, not a real name
reason.unusual_connection: Uses an unusual way to connect
reason.hidden_destination: Hides where the link really goes
reason.very_new_site: This site was created very recently
reason.scam_words: The address contains words scams often use
reason.carries_personal_data: The link carries your personal details in it
reason.long_complex_address: The address is unusually long and complex
reason.many_redirects: The link bounces through several sites
reason.risky_ending: Uses an ending that scams favor
reason.risky_registrar: Registered through a service scammers often use
reason.detector_suspicious: Our detector finds this site suspicious
reason.detector_safe: Our detector considers this site safe
reason.not_a_real_business: Not set up like a real company's site
reason.shifty_setup: The site keeps changing where it lives — a common scam trick
reason.padded_address: The address is padded with extra parts to hide the real name

update.optional_body: A newer version of Cleanway is out. Update to keep your protection current.
update.required_body: This version is out of date. Update Cleanway to keep your protection working.
